checks: The hypotheses of the frozen finite-tilt lemma match directly. The root equality is identical after multiplying by two, and q>0 and d≥2 give the equal positive volumes and proper endpoint cuts.

Each midpoint of captured endpoint points is in K by compatibility and on the captured side because the affine thresholds average to zero. Brunn–Minkowski bounds its midpoint body volume below by q and inclusion bounds it above by q.

If a compact convex subset omitted a point of the larger full-dimensional convex body, the positive distance to the smaller closed set and a short segment toward an interior point of the larger body would produce a positive-volume open ball in the difference. Thus the midpoint body equals the whole captured middle body.

The positive-volume Brunn–Minkowski equality case applies to the two full-dimensional compact convex caps. Their positive homothety factor is one by equality of volumes. See Figalli and Jerison, Quantitative stability for the Brunn–Minkowski inequality, §1, https://people.math.ethz.ch/~afigalli/papers-pdf/Quantitative-stability-for-the-Brunn-Minkowski-inequality.pdf. Compact convex bodies agreeing up to null sets agree as sets by the preceding argument.

A translation maps the minimizing-u face of one endpoint cap to that of the other. Properness ensures each face is the full cutting section and contains a relative open ball. Their (d−1)-volumes are positive and equal.

On each sign side, the proper endpoint planes admit interior points strictly on that side. Their midpoint obeys the corresponding strict middle inequality, and averaging interior balls places it in int K. The segment between the two interior midpoints crosses the middle plane in int K.

dependencies.mapping: Same three compact full-dimensional compatible bodies, same actual depth-attaining cap with u≠0 and the same captured-root equality. Its d>1, q>0 branch gives U=V=q=Q/3 and proper endpoint cuts.

overlap.comparison: In dimension two, (5)–(6) use the same finite strict saturation of one endpoint and the same fixed middle trace, so their comparison at an attaining cap implies both planar endpoint floors. They give no equal-volume tilt comparison, general-dimensional equality constraint, or automatic properness.

Its §2 first variation in the base coefficient would give equality of endpoint section areas by stationarity once all cuts are proper. That local formula assumes regular traces and does not give automatic properness, equal cap volumes, translation or midpoint set equality.

readability: The phrase “relative interior ball” is understood as a ball in the cutting hyperplane, obtained by intersecting that hyperplane with an interior ball of the original body.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: Positive critical root equality forces equal captured volumes and proper cuts, then equality in the midpoint comparison forces exact set equality and translated endpoint caps.
